title: Qatar Protectorate
capsule: Qatar came under a formal British protectorate relationship through the treaty of November 1916 with Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani, under which Britain assumed responsibility for Qatar's foreign affairs and defense in exchange for the ruling family's cooperation. The arrangement was similar to the Trucial States system, with Britain appointing a Political Agent in Doha from 1949. The discovery of oil in commercial quantities (Dukhan field, 1940; exports from 1949) transformed Qatar's economic prospects during the protectorate period. Britain revised its relationship with Qatar under the 1934 and subsequent agreements, and the protectorate status formally ended when Qatar declared full independence on 3 September 1971.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Qatar's territorial extent under the protectorate is moderately attested; land boundaries with Saudi Arabia and Bahrain remained disputed through the protectorate period and were only finally settled in 2001.
